correctness.rationale: With the previous nonempty complex K, any face using both new tips and any old vertex contains a directed 3-cycle, whereas either tip alone cones off all faces of K. The two cones form the suspension, with one extra edge attached at its distinct endpoints. The suspension is path connected and the endpoint attaching map is homotopic to a constant, so the edge adds one S^1. From the contractible middle simplex this inductively gives one sphere per degree 1 through r; no claim about an equivariant splitting is needed. An independent sign check uses the alternating trace on integral simplicial chains: an invariant face containing a reversed endpoint must contain its mate. Taking the outermost such pair forces the face to be exactly that edge since every other candidate vertex lies strictly inside the pair. Each reversed edge contributes +1 to the alternating trace (a transposition in degree 1), and the central simplex contributes 1 by contractibility. The resulting Lefschetz number r+1 saturates the sum of ranks, so every one-dimensional degree-d eigenvalue must be (-1)^d, including degree 1. After barycentric subdivision, a setwise-fixed simplex is pointwise fixed; the ordinary quotient has a cell for each simplex orbit, with rational chain complex the coinvariants. Coinvariants are exact over Q for a finite group by averaging and agree with invariants there. Hence precisely the even positive degrees survive in the quotient. This does not identify its integral homology. The supplied finite mod-two ranks and signed trace check were inspected, not executed or relied upon for the general result.

value.rationale: Nested pair reversals form a coherent family extending a two-fault homotopy classification. The arbitrary-depth integral action and ordinary quotient provide a concrete test family with an unbounded number of surviving degrees and a precise parity law, which is not captured by a list of nonequivariant homotopy types. This gives a useful symmetry-sensitive invariant without claiming quotient torsion or a full equivariant classification.
